title: Squirm
build: Mastertronic's original cassette of 1984 (1C 0003), a TAP of version 1 from the Ultimate Tape Archive on the Internet Archive, uta_Squirm_1984_Mastertronic_9165, MD5 3c85ddc4f4c605755f15d552e3e53457; loaded with the KERNAL's own tape routines (orientation.md)

credits.role: program: "an original game programmed by Tony Kelly", brought to Mastertronic by Mr Chip Software, as the Mastertronic Collectors Archive's review puts it; his initials, TK, are a character of the game's set and fill its high-score table

tools.emulator: VICE 3.10, the vice-mcp release v3.14.0, v3.14.0-linux-x86_64-gui.zip
tools.host: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, no display (cloud container)

accuracy.note: 60 of the listing's 337 comments, checked by a fresh agent that wrote none of them; all six wrong in a detail, none in the main claim
the page's sound players, run against the game's own sound code in the kit's 6502 for every button, each write to the sound chip compared jiffy by jiffy (test_sound.js)
the page's machine, which runs the game's own code for every widget: the first frame of play it draws compared pixel by pixel with VICE's (test_frame.js)
the whole game ported routine by routine and held in lockstep with the game's own code from the hand-over; the port showed no comment wrong

exclude: not used: BASIC's and the KERNAL's zero page, which the game neither reads nor writes
not used: the KERNAL's zero page, between the jiffy clock and the key number
not used: the KERNAL's zero page, between the key number and the game's pointers
not used: the byte after the game's pointers
not used: the KERNAL's other vectors and the tape buffer, which the game leaves alone
the screen at the hand-over: the READY prompt and the LOAD and RUN that VICE typed, which the title then covers; not part of the file
not the game's: the KERNAL's reset copies its table of vectors into the RAM under its own ROM here (the same 32 bytes as the ROM's table at $FD30)

regions: most of an assembler's BASIC program, saved with the game and never run
the assembler's BASIC arrays, saved with the game and never read
the assembler's BASIC arrays, saved with the game and never read
the start of try_cell, which is also the last character's shape
the bonus run's tune and the title tune's two voices
